edits.old: For scalar name values and an index {name: 1}, find({name: "Max"}, {_id: 0, name: 1}) is an illustrative covered query. An inclusion projection makes the required output fields explicit; merely excluding _id does not specify which other fields to return. (high confidence)
edits.new: For scalar name values and an index {name: 1}, find({name: "Max"}, {_id: 0, name: 1}) meets the documented covered-query conditions (query and returned fields all in the index, no null predicate, _id explicitly excluded), so it is an illustrative covered query. Excluding _id alone (projection {_id: 0}) does not make a query covered: the plan still fetches the document with all fields. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://dev.to/franckpachot/index-only-scan-on-json-documents-with-covering-and-multi-key-indexes-in-mongodb-53h4

edits.old: The idealo slow-operations profiler documents grouping operations by projected fields and reporting response bytes, index keys read, and documents read. These metrics help separate smaller responses from avoided document reads. Its README labels `rDocs = 0` as covered, but a MongoDB Community Forum reply notes that `totalDocsExamined: 0` can also occur when no results match; inspect the explain output and confirm the query returns matches before treating zero document reads as evidence of coverage. (low confidence)
edits.new: The idealo slow-operations profiler groups operations by fields including projected fields and reports response size in bytes, index keys read (rKeys), and documents read (rDocs). Its README labels rDocs = 0 as a "covered" query. A covered query is identified in explain by totalDocsExamined: 0 together with a non-zero totalKeysExamined, so zero document reads alone should be checked against keys examined and returned results. Sources: https://github.com/idealo/mongodb-slow-operations-profiler ; https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/easy-criterion-for-covered-queries-replacement-for-deprecated-indexonly/6125

evidence.quote: And last but not least, R/W shows metrics about how many index keys were read (rKeys), how many documents were read (rDocs) and written (wDocs)
If rDocs is 0 then the query was "covered" which means that all information needed could be retrieved from the index, thus no document had to be fetched into memory.
A covered query will have totalDocsExamined: 0 with a non-zero totalKeysExamined in the explain output.

edits.old: Coverage does not guarantee a fast query: a nonselective predicate can still examine many index keys. Compare keys examined, documents examined, returned rows, and measured runtime before treating a projection/index change as an efficiency improvement. (high confidence)
edits.new: Having an index does not guarantee efficiency: less selective queries match a larger percentage of documents and can't use indexes effectively, and when keys read is much higher than documents returned, the database is scanning many index keys. Compare keys examined, documents examined, returned rows, and measured runtime before treating a projection/index change as an improvement. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ ; https://github.com/idealo/mongodb-slow-operations-profiler
